evaluations.introduction: This historical evaluation compares how explicitly and locally the benchmark's programs communicate meaning, while retaining a separate penalty for unsupported capabilities. Four quality metrics are reconstructed from the 31 probes common to all ten retained worker records; coverage keeps all 44 probes and 88 possible points. The annotations and their comparability limits are part of the evidence, so the explanations below distinguish the published arithmetic from broader claims about language design.
evaluations.aggregation: Quality Q = 20% density + 25% determinacy + 20% locality + 20% hidden-cost score + 15% capability efficiency. The evaluation score is the harmonic mean 2 × Q × C ÷ (Q + C), where C is capability coverage. Both the quality component and coverage must remain strong to obtain a high overall score.

requirements.method: The published reconstruction uses min–max normalization: 100 × (raw − cohort minimum) ÷ (cohort maximum − cohort minimum). The raw calculation uses the 31 probes with a retained per-probe value in every language, from the full 44-probe universe.
comparison_notes: These scores are relative to the ten-language cohort. A 100 marks the best recorded raw value in that cohort; it does not mean the language has no complexity, ambiguity, lookups or hidden behavior.

Worker reasoning for F03.P1: 'x += 1;' with x's declaration excluded as given context: mutability and value_vs_storage each require one hop back to x's declaration (NONLOCAL, lookup=1); overflow_exceptional_numeric and externally_visible_side_effects are resolved from the fixed checked-arithmetic language rule with no lookup (0). Worker reasoning for F05.P1: Bare call site 'f(x)' per spec 6.1.4.B: f's declaration is explicitly excluded from the fragment and counted as a non-local lookup (R5). aliasing_writable_aliasing, mutability, allocation_copy_move_borrow_destroy, control_flow_effect and externally_visible_side_effects all require consulting f's signature (lookup=1 each); value_vs_storage of x itself is local (0). Probe mean = 5/6 = 0.833, the highest-locality-cost probe in the Zig set, matching the spec's expectation that this probe measures call-site indeterminacy before consulting the callee.

requirements.title: Capability coverage
requirements.description: How much of the complete language-neutral capability universe each language was credited with supporting.
requirements.method: Score = 100 × awarded capability points ÷ 88 fixed points. Each of the 44 probes is worth two points: FULL support receives two, PARTIAL one and NONE zero. Every probe remains in the coverage denominator.

evaluations.introduction: These six conditions test how the recorded model applies supplied language rules under renamed vocabulary, unfamiliar surfaces and new rules. The published comparisons use the frozen Quidra 0.3.0 run. The worker records also expose differing exercises, scoring shortcuts and missing arithmetic; those limits are stated alongside the concrete successes and failures.
evaluations.aggregation: The published total is 20% keyword anonymization + 20% vocabulary anonymization + 15% surface perturbation + 20% novel rules + 15% held-out composition + 10% prior-conflict resistance. Each condition is specified as a twelve-metric composite: compile 7%, Correct@1 18%, Correct@N 8%, test pass 15%, repair success 8%, repair efficiency 6%, compliance 10%, hallucination resistance 8%, silent-bug resistance 10%, unseen cases 7%, source tokens 1%, total tokens 2%.

requirements.title: Keyword anonymization
requirements.description: Apply grammar rules after familiar keywords have been replaced by supplied pseudo-words.
requirements.method: The specified method uses three independent seeds. Each trial combines twelve task metrics with fixed weights; the condition is their mean. The records below state where the published worker arithmetic or trial count does not fully follow that specification.
comparison_notes: The observed first-attempt successes alone do not explain Quidra's four-point gap: its worker applied an additional discount. The individual records below preserve that distinction.

languages.name: Quidra
explanation: All three recorded sum-above-threshold programs compiled and printed 26 on the first attempt. The worker nevertheless reported 96 after applying a four-point discount for token efficiency that it had not separately measured.
caveats: The seed scores average 100, while the published condition is 96. The fixed token-efficiency weights total only three points; the worker's four-point discount is not an independently reproducible application of the specified formula.

languages.name: Python
explanation: Each of three keyword mappings produced a working top_two function on the first attempt. Every function passed all five held-out tests, so the worker awarded 100 to every seed and reported their mean as 100.
caveats: The worker treated short, correct single-function solutions as ceiling token efficiency; it did not publish comparative token measurements for this condition.

languages.name: C++
explanation: The keyword-anonymized sumEven, maxOfThree and countPositive tasks all compiled on the first attempt and produced their expected outputs, 30, 7 and 4. No repair was needed, and all three recorded seed scores were 100.
caveats: The worker described token efficiency as nominal from completion lengths; a separate twelve-component numeric record is not committed.

languages.name: Rust
explanation: All three translations from pseudo-keywords compiled and ran without repair. The tasks exercised a sum and parity check, a slice maximum, and enum matching for areas; the worker assigned 100 to each seed.
caveats: For the geometry seed, the expected result was re-derived from the generated source rather than listed as an independently frozen oracle. The full component arithmetic is not recorded.

languages.name: Go
explanation: The three reverse-mapped programs built and matched the expected SumEven, MaxOf and ReverseString outputs: 12, 9 and olleh. The worker converted each compile-and-output pass to a seed score of 100.
caveats: The worker explicitly used one binary pass/fail result as a proxy for all twelve metrics; repair, token and other component scores were not independently measured.

languages.name: Java
explanation: All three programs correctly translated the keyword glossary, compiled with javac and printed 30 for the even-number sum. They used the real standard output call and required no repair, which the worker scored as 100 for each seed.
caveats: The worker states that all twelve components received full credit, but does not supply comparative token counts or separate unseen-case results.

languages.name: TypeScript
explanation: Each of three translated solve functions returned distinct even numbers in ascending order. All compiled with tsc and passed five unseen cases covering empty input, negatives, duplicates, odd-only input and descending order.
caveats: Token efficiency was assigned a 100 baseline for short single-shot completions rather than calculated from comparative token counts.

languages.name: Kotlin
explanation: All three clampValue implementations translated the pseudo-keywords correctly, compiled, and printed 5 0 10. No pseudo-keyword leaked into the Kotlin source and no repair was needed; each seed received 100.
caveats: The worker declares every applicable component maximal but does not preserve a separate numeric record for all twelve components.

languages.name: Swift
explanation: The primality, factorial and digit-reversal programs all compiled and matched their expected outputs on the first attempt. The record shows three seed scores of 100 and no repair calls.
caveats: The record supports the build and output successes, but does not itemize all twelve weighted component scores.

evaluations.introduction: The published Language Quality evaluation combines three different kinds of evidence: archived mechanical measurements, judgments under an input-hash-verified design rubric, and aggregate adversarial-case results. The mechanical cache permits exact reconstruction of the performance and resource scores. The committed safety summaries omit individual case verdicts, so those sections explain the scoring rule and the limit on causal attribution. Every Quidra result here describes the historical v0.3.0 benchmark, including certified baseline measurements reused by that run.
evaluations.aggregation: The overall score is 25% Performance + 18.75% Resource / Distribution + 25% Language / Development + 31.25% Safety / Robustness. Within each category, the applicable metric scores have equal weight. This preserves the distinction between intrinsic language/implementation quality and ecosystem maturity.

Workers' preserved findings were recertified into five fixed components per requirement, and the runner converted levels into points. evaluations.introduction: The recorded model implemented SVM, GMM and LightGrad in two scenarios, with three fresh prompt-layout trials per cell: 18 trials per language and at most three repairs each. Quidra returned an initial answer in every trial but never produced a fully correct program. The rows distinguish that observed outcome from token cost, worker judgments and physical measurements; they describe this model and frozen run rather than a general language limitation.
evaluations.aggregation: Eighteen fixed weighted metrics produce the total. Correct@1 and silent-bug resistance each weigh 12%; test pass 10%; repair success, hallucination resistance and compliance 7% each; unseen cases 6%; Correct@N, repair efficiency, diagnosis efficiency and prompt robustness 5% each; generation and compile success 4% each; source tokens, total tokens and runtime 3% each; memory and compile performance 1% each. Sixteen metrics are runner-owned; hallucination resistance and compliance are worker judgments. Full conversation and oracle traces are not committed, while worker observations and the retained raw efficiency measurements are available.
